messages:
Alyssa: FYI Acme POC asks for a simple pattern to allowlist traffic for our Dedicated endpoint. They want to lock down inbound on their side and also allow our callbacks to their webhook. Can we propose options?

Nick: Short answer: 3 options we usually offer.
- 1) Static EIP per Dedicated pool (preferred for enterprise POCs)
- 2) Customer-side proxy / reverse tunnel (if they'd rather keep no inbound traffic)
- 3) VPN/Private peering for fully private traffic

Alyssa: Great. Can you spell those out with next steps they can send to security?

Nick: Sure. I'll keep it short so they can paste into their firewall ticket.

Nick: Option A — Static EIP (fastest to onboard)
- We assign 1–4 dedicated static egress IPs for the pool used by the POC.
- Customer adds those IPs to their allowlist for inbound webhooks or IP-restricted app flows.
- Rotation: these IPs are stable for the duration of the reserved POC window (we can commit monthly).
- Action: I need a ticket to infra to reserve EIPs + an SOC contact for Acme to exchange IPs and SLA.

Nick: Example firewall entry they can copy:
```
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 198.51.100.23/32
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 198.51.100.24/32
```
(we'll replace the 198.51.100.x placeholders with real EIPs when allocated)

Jordan: Option B — Customer-managed forward proxy (no inbound allowlist on their perimeter)
- Customer runs a forward proxy/bastion that our Dedicated instances route outbound through (HTTP CONNECT or TLS tunnel).
- They only need to allow outbound from our pool to the proxy IP and we route callbacks through that proxy back to their systems.
- Good when security doesn't want external IPs hitting internal infra, or they need auditing inside their proxy.

Jordan: Quick example (customer firewall):
```
ALLOW TCP 3128 FROM 198.51.100.0/24   # allow Redwood to reach proxy
```
And the proxy will call internal endpoints which remain private.

Alyssa: Would that require more engineering on our side?

Nick: Minimal. We support configuring an HTTP/S proxy endpoint for a Dedicated pool. We can add the proxy host/port to the pool config and do a short smoke test (curl through proxy).

Maya: Option C — VPN / VPC Peering (most secure but higher setup)
- Establish site-to-site VPN or cloud VPC peering between Acme and Redwood Private infra.
- All traffic flows over private connectivity; no public allowlisting required.
- Longer lead time and networking approvals on both sides.

Jordan: For POC we usually start with A (Static EIP) unless the customer explicitly requires B/C. A gets them running same day once SOC adds IPs.

Alyssa: Acme also asked about locking API keys to source IPs on their side. Any constraints?

Nick: We don't support source-IP-scoped API keys from our hosted side today. For Dedicated you can pair keys with customer-side IP allowlisting at the customer firewall. If they need token scoping we can discuss a short-term canary feature (needs eng signoff).

Alyssa: They also have a security questionnaire item: can Redwood provide an SLA for static eips during the POC?

Nick: We can commit 'no-change' for the reserved POC window. I'll include that note in the infra ticket and copy legal if they want it in writing.

Alyssa: Nice. Can you add a short test snippet they can run once we give IPs?

Nick: Yep — we give them an endpoint and test curl for callback reachability. Example they can run from their firewall/test host to confirm we hit their webhook:
```
# from Redwood test runner (we'll run this)
curl -v -X POST https://acme.example.com/redwood-hook -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"event":"ping"}'
```
Or if they provide a proxy:
```
# from our Dedicated instance via proxy
curl -x http://proxy.acme.example.com:3128 -v https://internal.acme.example.com/health
```

InfraBot: INFRA-4567 created: Reserve 2 EIPs for sales POC (pool: dedicated-poc-acme). Owner: @Nick. ETA: 48h.

Jordan: Action items:
- Nick: open EIP reservation (done by InfraBot, link INFRA-4567) and reply with final IPs.
- Alyssa: send the three options to Acme and ask which they prefer. Note that B needs a proxy hostname, C needs VPN contact.
- Jordan: send a short pricing note for 2 reserved EIPs during POC (estimate added to quote).

Alyssa: I'll ping Acme now and ask which they want. I'll also include the firewall snippets.

Maya: Thanks — happy to jump on a 15 min network handoff call with Acme SOC once we have the EIPs.

Nick: If they prefer proxy route, loop me in — I'll help with proxy config and test script.

Alyssa: Perfect. I'll update thread after Acme replies. :thumbsup:
